task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You are unable to send MMS messages using your messaging app for the past few hours. You want to fix it and successfully send an MMS message.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hi there! I'm hoping you can help me out. For the past few hours I haven't been able to send picture messages — you know, MMS — from my messaging app. Regular texts seem to go through fine, but anything with a photo just won't send. It's been pretty frustrating.

turns.thought:
I'd be happy to help you get picture messaging working again. To get started, I'll need to look up your account.

Could you please provide your phone number (the one on your line), or your full name and date of birth?
turns.execution_output:
User: Sure! My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002.

I should also mention — I'm currently abroad in France, in case that matters for anything.

turns.thought:
Thanks! I found your account, John. Let me note a few things:

- Your line **555-123-2002** (L1002) is **Active** and **roaming-enabled**, with normal data usage (8.7 GB of 15 GB) — so nothing on the account or billing side should be blocking MMS.
- Your other two lines (555-123-2001 and 555-123-2003) aren't affected by this.

Since you're in France, roaming on your line is already enabled and you have data available. Now let's check a few settings on your device.

First, could you check what's showing in your **status bar** (the very top of your screen)? Just tell me what icons/symbols you see there — especially anything about signal strength, network type (5G/4G/3G), airplane mode, data, or Wi-Fi.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me take a look at my status bar.

turns.thought:
Yes — that's very likely the culprit! Airplane Mode disables all of your phone's wireless radios (cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth), so while it's on, your phone can't connect to the network at all. Interesting that regular texts appear to be going through — those may just be queued up and will send once you reconnect.

Please go ahead and turn **Airplane Mode OFF**:

1. Open **Settings** on your phone.
2. Tap **Airplane Mode** (it may also be called "Flight Mode" in some regions) and switch it **off**.
   - On many phones you can also swipe down from the top of the screen to open Quick Settings and just tap the airplane icon.

Once you've done that, wait about 30–60 seconds for your phone to reconnect, then take another look at your status bar and let me know:

- Do you now see **signal bars** and a **network type** (like 5G, LTE, or 4G)?
- Do you see any indication of **mobile data**, and whether **roaming** is indicated?

Since you're in France, we'll also want to make sure data roaming is switched on at the device level so your data (and MMS) works while abroad. Your line is already roaming-enabled on our side, so that part is good.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me turn airplane mode off.

turns.thought:
Great progress — you've got signal now. Three things need fixing, and all three matter for MMS:

**1. Turn Mobile Data ON** (currently disabled)
- Go to **Settings → Network & internet** (or "Connections")
- Tap **Mobile network**
- Switch **Mobile data / Cellular data** to **ON**

**2. Change your network mode off 2G**
- In the same **Mobile network** menu, tap **Network mode** (may be called "Preferred network mode" or "Network preference")
- Select **5G/LTE (4G) preferred** — this is usually the top option, sometimes labeled "5G/4G/3G auto"

This one is important: **MMS needs at least a 3G connection**, and 2G won't carry picture messages.

**3. Turn ON Data Roaming** (you're abroad in France)
- Still in **Mobile network**, tap **Roaming**
- Switch **Data roaming** to **ON**
- Your line is already roaming-enabled on our end, so this just switches it on at the device level

Go ahead and make those three changes, then tell me what your status bar shows again — I'd expect to see signal bars, a network type of 4G/5G or LTE, "Data Enabled," and possibly a roaming indicator. Let me know what you see.
turns.execution_output:
User: That's a lot of steps for me to juggle at once — I'm a bit worried about messing something up. Could you walk me through them one at a time? I can only really do one thing at a time on my end.

Which one should I do first — turning on mobile data, changing the network mode, or turning on data roaming?

turns.thought:
Absolutely, let's do them one at a time — no rush at all.

**Let's start with Mobile Data**, since that's the most fundamental one (without it, nothing data-related works, including MMS).

Please do this:

1. Open **Settings** on your phone.
2. Tap **Network & internet**  
   *(On Samsung phones this is called **Connections**; on iPhones it's **Cellular** or **Mobile Data**.)*
3. Tap **Mobile network** (on iPhone, skip this step).
4. Find the switch for **Mobile data** / **Cellular data** and toggle it **ON**.

**Tip:** On most Android phones you can also just swipe down twice from the top of the screen to open the full Quick Settings panel and tap the **Mobile data** tile directly — much quicker!

Take your time, and just let me know when it's on (or if it's already on). Then we'll move on to the next step. 😊
turns.execution_output: User: Okay, let me turn mobile data on.

turns.thought:
That's step one done ✅ — data is enabled.

**Next: let's get you off 2G.** This is likely the main reason your picture messages aren't going through, since 2G generally can't carry MMS at all.

Please do this:

1. Open **Settings**
2. Tap **Network & internet** *(on Samsung: **Connections**)*
3. Tap **Mobile network** *(this step is for Android; on iPhone tap **Cellular → Voice & Data**)*
4. Tap **Network mode** — it may also be called **Preferred network mode** or **Network preference**
5. Select the option that includes **5G and/or LTE (4G)**. It will usually look like one of these:
   - **5G/LTE preferred** ← best choice if you see it
   - **5G/4G/3G auto**
   - **4G (LTE) preferred**

It'll take a few seconds to register on the better network, and your signal bars may briefly disappear and come back — that's normal.

Take your time. When it's set, tell me what your status bar shows for signal strength and network type, and we'll move on to the roaming step.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me change the network mode now.

turns.thought:
Excellent — that's a huge improvement! 5G with 4 bars 🎉 You now have a strong network connection, which is exactly what MMS needs.

**Next step: turn ON Data Roaming** (since you're in France)

Please do this:

1. Open **Settings**
2. Tap **Network & internet** *(on Samsung: **Connections**)*
3. Tap **Mobile network**
4. Tap **Roaming** *(on some phones this is inside **Mobile network → Advanced**, or labeled **Data roaming**)*
5. Switch **Data roaming** to **ON**
   - If a warning pop-up appears about charges, tap **OK / Allow** to confirm.

Just to reassure you: your line **555-123-2002** is already roaming-enabled on our side, so turning this on at the device level gives you full data access while abroad.

On many Android phones there's also a shortcut: swipe down twice from the top for the full Quick Settings panel, and look for a **Roaming** tile — you can tap that directly if you see it.

Take your time, and let me know once it's on. Then we'll be in a good position to check whether MMS itself is working.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me turn on data roaming.

turns.thought:
Your connection looks great now — 5G, excellent signal, data enabled, roaming on. Before you try sending, let me have you run one quick check on your phone to confirm MMS is actually ready to go.

Please open your **messaging app** and use the built-in check: look for an option like **"Check MMS status"** or **"Can I send MMS?"**

*(If it helps: on Android, this is usually in **Messaging app → Settings → Advanced** or under **Chat features / MMS**; on iPhone, check **Settings → Messages → MMS Messaging** — make sure that toggle is ON.)*

Let me know what it reports — whether MMS is available or if there's any error — and then we'll do the real test send. 😊

Go ahead and give it a try.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check that for you.

turns.thought:
Good news: you now have all the prerequisites met (strong 5G signal, mobile data on, roaming on), so we've ruled out the connection side. Since MMS still isn't working, let's check the two most common remaining causes.

Let's take them one at a time, starting with:

**Step 1: Check your APN settings**

The APN (Access Point Name) tells your phone how to reach our data network, and it also contains the **MMSC URL** — the server that actually handles picture messages. If that's missing or wrong, MMS won't send even with perfect signal.

Please do this:
1. Open **Settings**
2. Tap **Network & internet** *(Samsung: **Connections**)*
3. Tap **Mobile network**
4. Tap **Access Point Names** (or **APN**)

Tell me:
- What **APN name** is currently selected/listed?
- Is there anything entered in the **MMSC** field? — it usually looks like a web address, e.g. `http://mms.example.com`

Take your time — once you tell me what you see there, we'll move on to the next check (Wi-Fi Calling, which can also interfere with MMS).
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check my APN settings.

turns.thought:
Good question — and yes, that's exactly the right instinct. Here's my read:

**Your APN looks fine.** The important part is that the **MMSC URL field isn't blank** — it's filled in with a properly-formed address (`http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc`). That's the field that, when missing, is one of the most common causes of exactly your symptom (regular texts work, pictures don't). Since yours is populated and your APN name is set to something valid ("internet"), I don't think this is your problem. 👍

So let's move on to the next check — **Wi-Fi Calling**.

**Why this matters:** In some cases Wi-Fi Calling can conflict with MMS, particularly when you're roaming internationally. It's worth switching off to rule it out.

Please do this:
1. Open **Settings**
2. Tap **Network & internet** *(Samsung: **Connections**)*
3. Tap **Wi-Fi Calling** *(on iPhone: **Settings → Phone → Wi-Fi Calling**)*

Please tell me:
- Is the **Wi-Fi Calling switch ON or OFF**?

Take your time. If it's **ON**, we'll turn it off and then re-test MMS. If it's already **OFF**, we'll move on to checking your messaging app's permissions.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check my Wi-Fi calling status.

turns.thought:
That's right — Wi-Fi Calling is off, so we can rule that out too. Good, we're narrowing things down.

**Next: let's check your messaging app's permissions.**

Your messaging app needs two specific permissions to send picture messages:
- **Storage** — to access the photo you're trying to attach
- **SMS** — to send the message itself

If either was denied or got turned off at some point, MMS can fail silently — which matches your symptom exactly.

Please do this:
1. Open **Settings**
2. Tap **Apps** (or **Apps & notifications**)
3. Find and tap your **Messages** app *(it may be called "Messaging" or "Messages")*
4. Tap **Permissions**

Then tell me what you see for **Storage** (might be called "Photos and videos" or "Files") and **SMS** — are they **Allowed** or **Denied** for each?

Take your time, and let me know what it shows. If any are denied, we'll turn them on and re-test. 😊
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check the messaging app's permissions.

turns.thought:
Yes — I think you've found it! 🔍

**Storage missing is very likely the problem.** When a permission isn't listed at all, it generally means the app has never been granted it. Your app can send and handle text (which is why **regular texts work fine**), but it has **no way to read the photo file** you're trying to attach — so the picture message fails every time. That matches your symptoms almost perfectly.

Let's grant it:

1. From that same **Permissions** screen, look for a way to add a permission — often **"See all permissions"**, **"Additional permissions"**, or a three-dot menu **(⋮)** in the top corner. Tap that.
2. Find **Storage** *(may appear as **Photos and videos**, **Files and media**, or **Photos**)*
3. Set it to **Allow** — you may see options like "Allow only while using the app" or "Allow all the time"; **"Allow all the time"** is the safest choice here so it works whenever you attach a photo.

Once that's done, please try sending a picture message again and let me know how it goes!

**One small thing to be aware of:** if it *still* doesn't work after granting storage, I'd suggest we try resetting your APN settings as a next step — even though the MMSC URL looked correct, a reset can repair settings that look fine but aren't behaving. But let's see how the permission change goes first. How does it look?
turns.execution_output: User: Let me grant the storage permission to the messaging app.
